# Chapter 1 — The Risk and AI Gap Part Seven Does Not Cover

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
Book 07 governed the policies that decide who may *act on* data — label, share, retain, discover. Book 07a governed where data *lives* — Fabric Domains and OneLake. This chapter opens the third half of the Purview surface: the solutions that decide who is *watched* (Insider Risk Management), who is *supervised* (Communication Compliance), and who is *exposed through AI* (DSPM for AI and Copilot). These are not access-control mechanisms; they are risk- and AI-posture mechanisms, and their fairness depends entirely on the organizational position they are scoped to. OrgPath is again the join key — but here it carries a heavier obligation, because mis-scoping these policies is not an outage, it is a surveillance error.
:::

## What Book 07 and Book 07a Each Closed, and What They Left Open

Establish the three-plane framing explicitly: user-policy plane (Book 07), data plane (Book 07a), and risk/AI plane (this book). The point is that Insider Risk Management, Communication Compliance, and Purview's AI-data-posture tooling are governed by neither of the two mechanisms already covered — they consume scope differently and they target a different question.

## Why Organizational Position Is the Right Scope for Risk and Surveillance

Argue the core thesis: a risk indicator that is normal for one segment is anomalous for another, and a supervisory obligation that is mandatory for one division is over-collection for another. Organizational position — not group membership, not job title strings — is the correct axis for differentiating risk posture, and OrgPath is the only attribute in the estate that carries it deterministically.

## The Asymmetry: These Policies Watch People, So Scoping Errors Are Surveillance Errors

Set up the guardrail thesis that the rest of the book returns to: mis-scoping a label policy is an inconvenience; mis-scoping an Insider Risk policy means watching people who should not be watched, or failing to watch people who should be. This raises the stakes on drift detection and on the privacy review that gates every reconciliation job in this book.

## OrgPath as the Join Key Across the Risk and AI Surfaces

Bridge to the rest of the book: the same OrgPath string that drives Adaptive Scopes in Book 07 also drives Insider Risk policy scoping, Communication Compliance policy scoping, and the data-asset boundaries that DSPM for AI reports against. Preview the reconciliation-job-and-drift-finding pattern the remaining chapters develop.
